page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-oriented virtual server deployed on KVM virtualization within the Cloud Native family. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs underpinned by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with shared CPU allocation. The instance provisions 48.0 GB of system memory, providing an expansive ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. The configuration does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external attached volumes for data persistence, and includes no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate competent burst performance balanced against shared-resource constraints. The platform attains a Geekbench single-core score of 2114.0 and a multi-core score of 6323.0, representing solid burst capability. Conversely, sustained stress-ng testing scores lower, reaching 787.09 in single-core and 3134.25 in multi-core metrics. Memory throughput exhibits a similar split: small-block cached read operations record 411.75 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes measure 35.68 GB/sec and 25.08 GB/sec respectively. PassMark database tests logged 2131.18 points, with Redis operations reaching 5.93 million operations per second.

Given its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and shared execution model, this instance provides cost-efficient memory density for workloads requiring vast address space without intensive per-core execution. The absence of integrated storage shifts the focus toward decoupled, memory-resident architectures. It is practical for distributed caching tiers, in-memory data structures, lightweight analytical staging, and memory-constrained microservices, while being less suited for sustained compute-heavy compilation or high-frequency local storage I/O.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is an x86_64 virtual instance tailored for memory-centric computing. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz across 4 shared vCPUs, it pairs moderate processing capability with an extensive 48.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, functioning entirely with remote network storage solutions. In benchmark testing, it displays respectable burst processing, achieving 2114.0 in Geekbench single-core and 6323.0 in multi-core tests, though sustained compute and uncached memory bandwidth reflect shared-resource limitations. Registering 5.93 million operations per second in Redis tests, this server delivers qualitative resource efficiency for memory-intensive operations. It is best configured for intermediate in-memory caching, memory-bound background tasks, and general microservices requiring substantial RAM headroom without demanding heavy continuous CPU throughput.
